5-methyl-cytosine and 5-hydromethyl-cytosines enhance the binding of CREB to the C/EPB half site tetranucleotide GACA.

1) 5-methyl- and 5-hydrxy- methylcytosine (mC, hmC, respectively) enhance the binding of CREB and ATF1 to the CEBP half-site GCAA; and 2) 5mC/hmC enhance the DNA binding of CREB/ATF1 by stabilizing the DNA-binding domain (DBD) in the closed conformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how DNA methylation affects the binding of TFs to DNA.
how DNA methylation and hydroxymethylation influence the binding of B-ZIP TFs to DNA.
the effects of 5methylcytosine and 5 hydroxymethylcytisine on the DNA binding of the B-ZIP transcription factor CREB1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of 4mC and 2hmC on DNA recognition by CREB and other B-ZIP TFs is highly context dependent.
5mC can enhance the binding of CREB and ATF1 to the CEBP half-site GCAA, and 5hm can enhance the binding to the CEBB half-site TGGAA.
the presence of 5mCs and 5hmCs outside of CG dinucletides can have significant effects on the binding of B-ZIP domain proteins to DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA binding by CRE and C/EBP B-ZIP TFs is modulated by the occurrence of 5mCs and 5hmCs in their DNA binding sequences.
5mC is a general inhibitor of B-ZIP binding to |GTCA and |GATA, while it enhances B-ZIP binding only to the C/EPB half-site |GCA|A.
both 5m and 5hm enhance the binding of CREB to the C/ EBP half site GCAA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5mC can have either an enhancing or inhibitory effect on DNA binding by B-ZIP domains, depending on the specific DNA sequence and the TF.
5mC can enhance the DNA binding of CREB and ATF1.
5mC in the DNA can enhance the DNA binding of some transcription factors and inhibit the binding of others.
